facts.heading: Anxiety worsening since September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and it has gotten worse since September.
facts.evidence: I'm not really sure where to start. I think I'm just anxious all the time, and it's got worse since September.

facts.heading: Made deputy head at school
facts.content: Hannah was made deputy head at her school. She has taught Year 4 for eleven years.
facts.evidence: I was made deputy head at my school. I've taught Year 4 for eleven years

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah worries that people will notice she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: But I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Thoughts occur Sunday evenings
facts.content: Hannah's anxious thoughts occur mostly on Sunday evenings. She rehearses for Monday's staff meeting.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing questions and reactions
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say. She imagines how others will think of her if she gets it wrong.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask, and what I'd say. Then what they'd think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Imagined negative thoughts
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth. She imagines they gave the job to a less capable teacher.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice Year 4 teacher who can't actually lead.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote an email to the governors four times. The email was about a change to the behaviour policy.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times. A change to the behaviour policy.

facts.heading: Fear of seeming stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr Hargreaves would think she was stupid regarding the email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr Hargreaves' reaction
facts.content: Mr Hargreaves has been kind to Hannah. He told her in September he was delighted.
facts.evidence: He's been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling of lying
facts.content: Hannah feels she is lying to Mr Hargreaves about her capabilities.
facts.evidence: That makes it worse somehow, because I feel I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Pretending to be capable
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is pretending to be someone who knows what she is doing.
facts.evidence: About being capable. As if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Comparing to mother's career
facts.content: Hannah compares her work to her mother's career as a headteacher. She thinks everything she does would have been done better by her mother.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's reputation
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a brilliant headteacher. People in the village still praise her.
facts.evidence: She was brilliant. Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Mother's retirement
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago. A library has been named after her.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they've named a library after her.

facts.heading: Mother's feedback
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has always worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Feeling of making a fuss
facts.content: When her mother gives this feedback, Hannah feels like she is making a fuss.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel I'm making a fuss.

facts.heading: Withholding bad news
facts.content: Hannah does not tell her mother how bad things are.
facts.evidence: So I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking up at four AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning. She goes through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine, then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Waking due to worries
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four to deal with various worries. These worries include timetable changes, Ofsted prep, a parent complaint, and a child she is worried about.
facts.evidence: Timetable changes, the Ofsted prep, a parent complaint, a child I'm worried about. It goes round and round.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption for energy
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day.
facts.evidence: Five or six.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences physical symptoms in the afternoons when she cannot sit still. Her heart goes fast and her hands shake.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water due to physical symptoms.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.

facts.heading: Partner's reaction to advice
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when her partner Ben suggests she should enjoy her situation.
facts.evidence: Guilty, and a bit alone. He means well.

facts.heading: Partner's profession and view
facts.content: Ben is an engineer and believes that if something is a problem, it can be fixed.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer, he thinks if something's a problem you fix it.

facts.heading: Difficulty with social connections
facts.content: Hannah does not have friends at school to talk to anymore. She used to eat lunch in the Year 4 corridor with them.
facts.evidence: Not any more, not really. I used to eat lunch in the Year 4 corridor with the others.

facts.heading: Loss of social group
facts.content: Hannah lost friends and company along with her promotion. She misses her class and the children.
facts.evidence: Yes. I hadn't thought of it like that. I miss them. I miss my class too.

facts.heading: Missing children's experiences
facts.content: Hannah misses the daily experience of children getting something for the first time. Her days are now spreadsheets.
facts.evidence: The children, honestly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time. Now my days are spreadsheets.

facts.heading: Desire for promotion
facts.content: Hannah thought she wanted the promotion and said yes because she could not say no to the head.
facts.evidence: I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Tears about future prospects
facts.content: Hannah cried after saying yes to the promotion because of fear and the feeling she would never get to go back.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I'd never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays when they went walking in the Lakes.
facts.evidence: The summer holidays. We went walking in the Lakes, and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Pre-term distress
facts.content: The week before term, Hannah was a wreck and could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before term I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A child laughing, a good email. It helped for about two weeks and then I stopped, because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Stopped writing due to feeling silly
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing because she felt silly about it. She felt like she was bragging to herself.
facts.evidence: I stopped, because I felt silly. As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook.

facts.heading: Wants to avoid feeling like a fraud
facts.content: Hannah wants to do her job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: I'd like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Goal for Tuesday at work
facts.content: Hannah wants to walk into a meeting without rehearsing it first. She wants to send an email only once.
facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing it first. Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal for Sunday evening
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without her stomach in knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feeling lighter after sharing
facts.content: Hannah felt lighter and a bit tearful after stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: First time sharing bad news
facts.content: Hannah has not told anyone how bad her situation is. She has not told Ben about the four a.m. issue.
facts.evidence: That it's the first time I've told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows about the four a.m.

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah feels scared about telling Ben how bad things are. She worries he would be hurt that she didn't say sooner.
facts.evidence: Scary. He'd probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Need for quiet moment to share
facts.content: Hannah needs a quiet moment to tell Ben. She is too wound up on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment. Not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too wound up.

facts.heading: Preferred time to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah suggested Saturday morning over breakfast to tell Ben. She noted he is always in a good mood then.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps? He's always in a good mood then.

facts.heading: Intends to try notebook again
facts.content: Hannah agreed to try the evening notebook again for a week. She plans to put it by the kettle to avoid forgetting.
facts.evidence: I could. I'll put it by the kettle so I don't forget.

facts.heading: Nearly cancelled session this morning
facts.content: Hannah nearly cancelled the session this morning. She is glad she did not cancel.
facts.evidence: Only that I nearly cancelled this morning. I'm glad I didn't.
